researchers.name: Natalija Fejsa
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.bio: Natalija Fejsa received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Mathematics and Computer Science from the University of Novi Sad in 2009 and 2011, respectively, and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Ljubljana in 2016, with a thesis on certified compilation passes in the Coq proof assistant. After a two-year postdoctoral appointment at the University of Innsbruck, she returned to Novi Sad in 2018 as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Informatics. Her group works on mechanically verified compilers, dependent type theory, and the construction of large-scale machine-checked proofs of correctness for software toolchains. She teaches courses on logic, formal methods, and functional programming. The group uses the Coq and Agda proof assistants and maintains a small server cluster for batch proof checking.
open_to: joint projects with companies requiring formal correctness guarantees for safety-critical software
contract research on formal verification of compiler passes or static analyzers
consulting on the applicability of proof assistants to industrial software verification
student internships involving Coq or Agda formalization work
co-supervision of industrial Ph.D. students working on certified toolchains
researchers.industry_experience: Natalija Fejsa participated in a short consulting engagement in 2022 with a regional automotive software supplier interested in formal verification tooling, contributing a feasibility assessment for applying certified compilation to their code-generation pipeline.
researchers.notes: Natalija Fejsa is interested in collaborating with NTP companies working on safety-critical embedded systems, compilers, or developer tooling, particularly where correctness guarantees are legally or contractually required. Her group's workload allows for one new collaboration starting in late 2026.

researchers.name: Velimir Mladenović
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation
researchers.bio: Velimir Mladenović received his Dipl.Ing. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2003 and his Ph.D. in Mechatronics from the same institution in 2010, with a dissertation on formal fault propagation models for pneumatic control loops in process plants. He joined the Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation at the Faculty of Technical Sciences as an Assistant Professor in 2011 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2017. His group works on functional safety assessment, HAZOP methodology, and the modelling of hybrid pneumatic-electronic control architectures in compliance with IEC 61511 and IEC 61508. He teaches Industrial Automation Safety and Process Control Systems at both undergraduate and graduate level. The group regularly uses a pilot-scale process control rig, fault injection testbeds, and MATLAB/Simulink together with specialised safety analysis tools including XFMEA and PHA-Pro.
open_to: contract research on HAZOP studies and SIL verification for industrial clients
joint projects with NTP Novi Sad companies working on process automation or safety systems
industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed in process safety roles
consulting on IEC 61511 safety lifecycle documentation and management of change
student internships at companies with safety instrumented systems or process control infrastructure
equipment access to process control rig and fault injection testbed for collaborative experiments
researchers.industry_experience: Mladenović has conducted HAZOP studies and SIL verification assignments as an independent expert for four process industry clients in Serbia and one in Croatia since 2013, covering natural gas, refining, and pharmaceutical intermediate manufacturing. He holds a TÜV Rheinland Functional Safety Engineer certificate (process sector), renewed in 2022.
researchers.notes: Actively seeking industry contacts at NTP Novi Sad with automation or process safety products; prefers collaborative arrangements where plant access or failure data can be exchanged. Currently co-supervising two PhD students whose stipends are partially funded through the SAFEPNEU project; capacity for a third doctoral student exists from 2025 onward.

researchers.name: Bogdan Milošević
researchers.title: Senior Research Associate
researchers.bio: Bogdan Milošević completed his BA and MA in English Language and Literature at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Philosophy, and received his PhD from the same institution in 2013 with a dissertation on representations of land degradation in Nigerian fiction of the 1970s and 1980s. He joined the Department of English Studies as a Research and Teaching Assistant in 2013 and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2020. His work sits at the intersection of ecocriticism, postcolonial literary theory, and Anglophone West African prose, with recurring attention to oil extraction, agrarian displacement, and climate precarity as literary themes. He teaches undergraduate and postgraduate courses in postcolonial literatures and critical theory. His research relies primarily on archival materials, published literary corpora, and discourse analysis tools available through the faculty library consortium.
open_to: joint projects with organisations working on environmental communication or sustainability reporting who need humanistic analysis of narrative and framing
consulting on intercultural communication contexts involving Anglophone African texts or discourse
student internships related to corpus annotation or literary data organisation
researchers.notes: Milošević's expertise is firmly in literary and humanistic analysis; potential collaborations with technology companies would need to involve a clear humanistic component such as text analysis, narrative framing research, or cultural communication consulting. He has expressed interest in corpus linguistics collaborations that might support larger-scale analysis of literary environmental language.

researchers.name: Lucia Hriešiková
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.bio: Lucia Hriešiková completed her BSc in Biology at the University of Novi Sad (2002) and her PhD in Plant Ecophysiology at Charles University, Prague (2008), with a dissertation on water-stress responses in temperate mosses. After a two-year postdoctoral position at the University of Ljubljana, she returned to Novi Sad and joined the Department of Biology and Ecology, where she became Associate Professor in 2018. Her group studies how bryophytes and biological soil crusts (BSCs) survive extreme desiccation and UV exposure in Pannonian steppe and loess habitats, combining ecophysiological measurements, pigment biochemistry, and controlled desiccation–rehydration experiments. She teaches Plant Physiology and Ecology of Extreme Environments at undergraduate and postgraduate level. The group uses a climate-controlled desiccation chamber, portable gas-exchange analysers, fluorescence imaging, and HPLC for pigment and antioxidant profiling.

researchers.industry_experience: Hriešiková provided informal technical advice to a regional environmental consultancy preparing a loess habitat restoration plan for a road-construction mitigation project in 2020, though this did not result in a formal contract.
researchers.notes: Her primary interest in industry collaboration is in applied soil restoration and biocrust biotechnology; she is cautious about engagements that would require diverting significant equipment time away from ongoing grant work. She is open to co-supervising industrial PhD candidates if the topic is directly relevant to BSC ecophysiology or stress biology applications.

researchers.name: Andrija Zarić
researchers.title: Research Associate
researchers.bio: Andrija Zarić completed his undergraduate studies in Digital Art and Multimedia at the Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad in 2009, followed by a Master's degree in Performance Studies at the Faculty of Music and Performing Arts, Brno, Czech Republic (2012). He received his PhD from the University of Novi Sad in 2018 with a dissertation on proprioceptive feedback loops in interactive stage environments. Since 2019 he has held a Research Associate position at the Department of Digital Arts. His research focuses on the integration of wearable biosensors—EMG, heart rate variability, and inertial measurement units—into live performance contexts, using the captured physiological data to drive real-time generative visual systems. He teaches courses in interactive media and physical computing. The group regularly uses the department's motion-capture studio and a small electronics prototyping lab equipped with microcontroller platforms and custom sensor rigs.
open_to: joint projects with companies developing wearable health or fitness sensors who need performance/experience design input

researchers.industry_experience: Zarić completed a short consultancy engagement in 2020 with a Novi Sad-based rehabilitation technology startup, advising on how real-time biofeedback visualisations could be made more engaging for patients in post-stroke movement therapy sessions. The collaboration did not result in a commercial product but informed his subsequent research on EDA and skin conductance in movement contexts.
researchers.notes: Zarić is particularly interested in connecting with companies in health technology, rehabilitation, and interactive installation design where his biosensor and real-time visualisation expertise has direct application beyond the arts. He has no current sabbatical plans and carries a moderate teaching load. He prefers collaborations that allow for artistic or research publication outputs alongside any commercial deliverables.

researchers.name: Dejan Hadžić
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications
researchers.bio: Dejan Hadžić received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2004 and 2007 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2013. He was appointed Assistant Professor in 2014 and promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. His research centres on soft-switching resonant converter topologies—particularly LLC and CLLC variants—and frequency-domain methods for modelling conduction, switching, and magnetic losses in medium-power isolated DC-DC stages intended for battery and supercapacitor interfaces. The group routinely uses a Chroma programmable DC source, a Keysight impedance analyser, a custom calorimetric loss bench, and a dSPACE rapid-control-prototyping system. He teaches power electronics and electronic circuit design at undergraduate and master level.

The calorimetric bench is available for external measurements by arrangement but has limited booking slots during the teaching semester (October–January and March–June).

researchers.name: Lidija Radić
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry
researchers.bio: Lidija Radić completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Chemical Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2003 and 2005 respectively, followed by a PhD in Pharmaceutical Solid-State Chemistry at the same institution in 2010. She joined the Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry as a teaching assistant in 2006 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2018. Her research group investigates the solid-state landscape of active pharmaceutical ingredients, with particular focus on co-crystal screening, polymorph identification, and crystal engineering strategies to enhance dissolution rate and bioavailability. She teaches courses in Physical Chemistry of Materials and Instrumental Methods of Analysis. The group routinely operates a powder X-ray diffractometer (Bragg-Brentano geometry), a DSC-TGA platform, and a confocal Raman mapping system acquired in 2017.

She has also provided ad hoc analytical consultancy to two smaller regional generic manufacturers.
researchers.notes: Radić has expressed interest in longer-term engagement with companies at NTP Novi Sad, particularly those working in generic pharmaceutical development or nutraceutical formulation. Her laboratory has some remaining instrument capacity on the Raman mapping system on Fridays and can accommodate external samples with reasonable lead time. She is not planning a sabbatical in the near term.

researchers.name: Luka Fejsa
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.department: Department of Chemistry, Biochemistry and Environmental Protection
researchers.bio: Luka Fejsa completed his BSc and MSc in Chemistry at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, followed by a PhD in Environmental Chemistry defended in 2016 at the same institution, with a dissertation on biosorption of cationic dyes onto sunflower and corn by-products. After a postdoctoral stay at the Faculty of Technology, University of Maribor (2017–2018), he returned to Novi Sad as a teaching assistant and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2021. His group investigates low-cost biosorbents derived from agricultural lignocellulosic residues, focusing on surface chemistry, isotherm and kinetic modelling, and column dynamics. He teaches undergraduate courses in Analytical Chemistry and Environmental Protection Chemistry. The group routinely uses FTIR, XPS, SEM-EDX, and batch equilibrium setups available at the Faculty of Sciences analytical laboratories.

researchers.name: Luka Ranković
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.department: Department of Field and Vegetable Crops
researchers.bio: Luka Ranković completed his BSc and MSc degrees in Plant Protection at the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, graduating with an MSc thesis on acetolactate synthase (ALS) inhibitor resistance in Amaranthus retroflexus in 2012. He received his PhD from the same faculty in 2017, focusing on combined target-site and metabolic resistance mechanisms in common weeds from Vojvodina arable fields. He joined the Department of Field and Vegetable Crops as a teaching assistant in 2017 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2021. His group characterises herbicide-resistant biotypes collected from sunflower, soybean, and maize fields, using enzyme assays, whole-plant dose–response bioassays, and gene sequencing. He teaches Weed Science and Crop Protection Practicals. The group works in the Faculty herbology laboratory and uses an HPLC system and real-time PCR platform for resistance diagnostics.

researchers.name: Danica Pantelić
researchers.title: Professor Emeritus
researchers.bio: Danica Pantelić received her BSc in Mathematics and Computer Science from the University of Novi Sad in 1983 and her PhD in Educational Informatics from the same university in 1994. She spent her entire academic career at the Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' in Zrenjanin, rising to Full Professor in 2003 and retiring as Professor Emeritus in 2018. Her research focused on the design and evaluation of computer-assisted language learning systems, with particular attention to rule-based and later data-driven difficulty scaling, point economies, and progress-feedback loops. She taught courses in human–computer interaction and educational software design. Her group used a small usability laboratory equipped with screen-recording and eye-tracking apparatus, and maintained partnerships with secondary schools in the Zrenjanin municipality for longitudinal user studies.

researchers.notes: Retired; not available for project leadership or supervision of PhD students. Willing to consult on the design or evaluation of adaptive difficulty systems, gamification reward structures, or language learning platform assessments, particularly for regional or multilingual contexts. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an Assistant Professor in 2014 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. His group focuses on explainability and fairness of machine learning models used in high-stakes domains such as credit scoring, hiring, and clinical triage. He teaches courses on machine learning, software engineering, and applied statistics. The group uses a local GPU cluster and licensed access to several anonymised administrative datasets through institutional agreements.

researchers.name: Dejan Bogdanović
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Dejan Bogdanović is a Full Professor in the Department of Production Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. His research focuses on additive manufacturing and design optimization, with particular emphasis on selective laser melting of metallic alloys, porosity reduction strategies, topology optimization, and the design of support structures for metal 3D printing. He has contributed significantly to developing process parameter methodologies that improve part quality in powder-bed fusion technologies and has advanced constraint-based topology optimization frameworks suitable for direct manufacture. Professor Bogdanović holds a patent on lattice support structures and has published extensively in leading journals and conferences. He is open to industrial PhD supervision and collaborative projects with industry partners seeking to integrate advanced manufacturing solutions.

researchers.name: Ondrej Turčan
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.bio: Ondrej Turčan completed his undergraduate and MSc studies in biology at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, graduating in 2003 and 2006 respectively. He obtained his PhD in plant cytogenetics at the University of Novi Sad in 2011, with a dissertation on polyploid complexes in Balkan endemic Centaurea. After a postdoctoral stay at the Institute of Botany of the Czech Academy of Sciences in Brno (2012–2014), he returned to Novi Sad where he is now Associate Professor. His group focuses on chromosome evolution, karyotype architecture, and repetitive DNA dynamics in polyploid Balkan endemic plants, using fluorescence in situ hybridisation (FISH), flow cytometry, and bioinformatic analysis of repeat families. He teaches genetics and cell biology at undergraduate level and plant molecular systematics at MSc level. The laboratory is equipped with an epifluorescence microscope with digital imaging, a flow cytometer, and standard molecular biology infrastructure.

researchers.name: Jelena Đukić

researchers.department: Department of Civil Engineering and Geodesy
researchers.bio: Jelena Đukić received her BSc and MSc degrees in Civil Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2005 and 2008 respectively, and her PhD from the same institution in 2013, with a dissertation on fragility curve derivation for unreinforced masonry buildings in the Pannonian region. Her research group focuses on probabilistic seismic risk assessment of existing masonry building stocks, empirical and analytical fragility modelling, and urban-scale loss estimation. She teaches courses in structural mechanics and earthquake engineering. The group uses TREMURI and OpenSees for nonlinear structural analysis, and collaborates with the Institute of Architecture and Urban Planning of Vojvodina for building inventory data.

researchers.bio: Aleksandar Bošković received his Dipl.Ing. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2004 and his PhD from the same institution in 2011, with a thesis on residual stress formation in injection-moulded semi-crystalline thermoplastics. The group works primarily with commercial FEA and injection moulding simulation packages, and has access to a materials testing laboratory with DSC, tensile testing frames, and coordinate measuring equipment for warpage validation.

researchers.name: Jasmina Filipović
researchers.title: Teaching Assistant
researchers.bio: Jasmina Filipović completed her undergraduate and master's studies in psychology at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2021. She joined the Department of Psychology as a Teaching Assistant in 2022, where she works under the supervision of Associate Professor Dragan Milošević. Her research focuses on psychophysiological correlates of emotion regulation difficulties in individuals with subclinical perfectionism, with particular attention to skin conductance response, cardiac vagal tone, and respiratory sinus arrhythmia recorded during evaluative stress tasks. The group uses a BIOPAC MP160 system and standardised laboratory stress protocols. She teaches courses in physiological psychology and research methods. She is currently enrolled in the doctoral programme at the same faculty.
open_to: joint projects

student internships in laboratory settings
consulting on study design for stress measurement
equipment access for partners needing BIOPAC-based physiological recording
researchers.notes: Filipović is in the early stages of her doctoral work and takes on external collaborations only with supervisor approval. She has hands-on expertise with BIOPAC MP160 signal acquisition and basic signal processing in AcqKnowledge; she does not yet have experience with clinical populations or intervention designs.

researchers.name: Anna Kmeťová
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Anna Kmeťová received her BSc and MSc in Mathematics from the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, in 2001 and 2003 respectively, and her PhD in Computer Science from the University of Ljubljana in 2008, with a dissertation on metaheuristic approaches to combinatorial optimisation. She joined the Department of Mathematics and Informatics at the University of Novi Sad in 2009 and was promoted to Full Professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, neural architecture search, and the deployment of compact neural networks on microcontrollers and edge devices. She teaches courses in algorithms, computational intelligence, and machine learning. The group regularly uses the Faculty's embedded systems laboratory, equipped with ARM Cortex-M development boards and FPGA prototyping platforms, as well as cluster computing resources shared across the Faculty.
open_to: joint projects with companies developing embedded sensing or monitoring products

researchers.industry_experience: Kmeťová served as a technical consultant to a Novi Sad-based startup developing predictive maintenance firmware for 18 months during 2019–2020, contributing to the design of their on-device inference pipeline. She has supervised two MSc theses co-defined with local technology companies through the NTP Novi Sad student programme.
researchers.notes: Kmeťová is active in the CROSSEDGE project through 2026 and prefers new collaborations that can be aligned with its industrial IoT and smart manufacturing scope. She is particularly interested in partners who can provide real sensor data from production environments, as access to such data is a consistent bottleneck for her group. She has no current sabbatical plans.

researchers.name: Bojana Rajić
researchers.title: PhD student
researchers.bio: Bojana Rajić completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Management at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2022. She enrolled in the doctoral programme the same year and is currently in the third year of her PhD, working under the supervision of Associate Professor Dragan Milošević. Her research focuses on why employees at small and medium-sized enterprises in Western Balkan transition economies accept or resist digital transformation initiatives, drawing on organisational behaviour theories and survey-based methods. She participates in undergraduate teaching exercises in Organisational Behaviour and Strategic Management. For her work she uses SPSS, SmartPLS, and ATLAS.ti, and accesses the Faculty's computer lab for large-scale survey processing.

researchers.notes: Bojana is in the writing-up phase of her PhD and expects to defend in 2026; she is available for collaboration but has limited time for large new commitments before submission. She is particularly interested in connecting with NTP companies that are actively implementing ERP, CRM, or workflow automation tools and would welcome access to their employees as survey respondents.

researchers.name: Ivana Ljubojević
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.bio: Ivana Ljubojević completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Chemical Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2009 and 2011 respectively. She received her PhD in Pharmaceutical Biotechnology from the same faculty in 2016, with a dissertation on lipase-mediated synthesis of phosphatidylcholine analogues for liposomal formulations. After a two-year postdoctoral stay at the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Ljubljana, she returned to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor in 2019. Her group focuses on enzymatic routes for producing high-purity phospholipids, their incorporation into liposomal carrier systems, and downstream purification by preparative chromatography. She teaches Biochemical Engineering and Pharmaceutical Formulation Technology. The group routinely uses a 5 L stirred-tank bioreactor, HPLC-ELSD, GC-MS, dynamic light scattering, and a mini-extruder setup for liposome preparation.

researchers.notes: Ljubojević is particularly interested in connecting with companies at NTP Novi Sad that manufacture or formulate lipid-based products, including nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and generic pharmaceuticals. She is on reduced teaching load in the 2025–2026 academic year and can take on one additional collaboration.

researchers.name: Nina Ljubojević
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.bio: Nina Ljubojević completed her medical degree at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad in 2004, followed by a neurology residency at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. She received her PhD in 2012 on interictal epileptiform discharge patterns during non-REM sleep and was appointed Associate Professor in 2020. Her group focuses on polysomnographic characterisation of sleep macro- and microarchitecture in patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, examining how epileptiform activity interacts with sleep spindles, slow oscillations, and arousal indices across sleep stages. She teaches clinical neurology and neurophysiology at undergraduate and postgraduate level. The group operates a dedicated sleep laboratory equipped with 32-channel EEG-polysomnography, and collaborates with the epilepsy monitoring unit at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina.

researchers.notes: Dr Ljubojević is on parental leave until September 2025 and will have limited availability for new commitments before that date; she has indicated openness to preliminary discussions during this period. She prefers collaborations that involve access to clinical patient cohorts rather than purely computational or animal-model work.

researchers.name: Dimitrije Vučković
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.department: Department of Energy and Process Engineering
researchers.bio: Dimitrije Vučković received his Dipl.Ing. and M.Sc. degrees from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2001 and 2005 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2010, with a thesis on dynamic modelling of organic Rankine cycle systems for low-grade heat sources. He has been a Full Professor in the Department of Energy and Process Engineering since 2019. His research group focuses on transient and steady-state simulation of ORC units, working-fluid screening, expander characterisation, and model-based control design. He teaches thermodynamics, process simulation, and energy conversion systems at undergraduate and postgraduate level. The group operates a small-scale ORC test rig (nominal 5 kWe) and uses Modelica-based simulation platforms alongside in-house MATLAB toolchains for working-fluid property calculations and controller tuning.

researchers.notes: Vučković is interested in applications where dynamic behaviour or variable heat-source conditions are central; he is less interested in purely economic or lifecycle-assessment studies without a technical modelling component. The laboratory ORC rig is available for external collaborative use subject to scheduling; external users should expect three to four months lead time for access. He is not on sabbatical and has capacity for one new substantial collaboration starting in 2025 or 2026.

researchers.name: Teodora Jakovljević
researchers.title: Senior Research Associate
researchers.bio: Teodora Jakovljević completed her BSc and MSc in Agricultural Engineering at the University of Novi Sad (2007, 2010), followed by a PhD in Precision Agriculture Systems at the same institution (2015), with a dissertation on closed-loop spray control for tractor-mounted variable-rate applicators. Since 2016 she has been a Senior Research Associate within the Agricultural Robotics Group at BioSense Institute, where the team develops autonomous aerial and ground platforms for field-scale crop monitoring and site-specific input management. Her own work focuses on integrating multispectral and LiDAR canopy data acquired during UAV flights into real-time actuator feedback loops for variable-rate application of fertilisers and pesticides. She co-supervises MSc students through the Faculty of Technical Sciences and regularly uses the group's UAV flight cell, spectral calibration laboratory, and HIL actuator test rig.

She participated in a short industry secondment at an agricultural drone service provider in Subotica during the 2022 growing season to observe operational deployment conditions.
researchers.notes: Jakovljević is co-supervising two PhD students who are expected to defend in 2026, which limits availability for new large project commitments until late that year. She has expressed interest in connecting with companies developing embedded compute solutions or miniaturised LiDAR sensors suitable for UAV payloads. The HIL test bench at BioSense Institute is available for external use subject to scheduling.

researchers.name: Ildikó Papp
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Graphic Engineering and Design
researchers.bio: Ildikó Papp received her Dipl.Ing. in Graphic Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2003, and her PhD in Technical Sciences from the same institution in 2010, with a dissertation on constraint-based layout optimization for multipage print documents. She joined the Department of Graphic Engineering and Design as an assistant professor in 2011 and was promoted to associate professor in 2017. Her research group focuses on computational methods for automating graphic reproduction workflows, including parametric dieline construction, artwork-to-substrate registration algorithms, and color-managed PDF processing pipelines. She teaches courses in prepress technology and digital color management. The group regularly uses spectrophotometric and densitometric measurement equipment and maintains a digital proofing laboratory with calibrated wide-format inkjet output.

researchers.name: Radovan Bajić

Od 2017. godine zaposlen je kao asistent profesor na istom fakultetu. Njegova istraživačka grupa bavi se agent-baziranom simulacijom organizacionih procesa, posebno dinamikom kompetencija i prenosa znanja u postmerger integracijama manufacturing preduzeća. Nastavu drži iz predmeta Simulacija poslovnih sistema i Organizaciono ponašanje. U radu koristi platforme AnyLogic i NetLogo, kao i laboratoriju za sistemsku dinamiku FTN-a.

Trenutno vodi jedan aktivni međunarodni projekat (SIMORG, do kraja 2025), pa je kapacitet za nove veće projekte ograničen do 2026. godine.

researchers.name: Tihomir Pekez
researchers.title: Teaching Assistant
researchers.bio: Tihomir Pekez completed his undergraduate and master's studies in Media Studies at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, graduating with a master's thesis on visual irony in Serbian political satire in 2022. He joined the department as a Teaching Assistant in 2023. His research focuses on the semiotics of political meme circulation on domestic social platforms, with particular attention to visual rhetoric, irony, and affective registers in Serbian online public spheres. He works within a small research group studying digital political communication in post-Yugoslav contexts. He teaches courses on media semiotics and digital culture. For his empirical work he uses social media scraping tools, corpus annotation software, and qualitative image analysis frameworks, typically sharing university computing infrastructure.

researchers.notes: Pekez is in the early stages of his PhD and his availability for large external commitments is limited. He is most useful to industry partners who need expertise in qualitative and semiotic analysis of Serbian-language digital content rather than large-scale quantitative data infrastructure.

researchers.name: Ljubomir Orlović
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.bio: Ljubomir Orlović completed his undergraduate and master's studies in Chemical Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2008 and 2010 respectively. He obtained his PhD in Pharmaceutical Engineering from the same institution in 2015, with a dissertation on multivariate monitoring of aqueous film-coating processes. He joined the Department of Pharmaceutical Engineering as a Teaching Assistant in 2011 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2017. His group focuses on applying design of experiments, principal component analysis, and multivariate statistical process control to solid dosage manufacturing, particularly pan coating and fluidised-bed coating unit operations. He teaches courses in pharmaceutical process engineering and quality-by-design. The group regularly uses a Glatt GPCG-1 laboratory fluidised-bed coater, a Bohle pan coater, and near-infrared and Raman in-line probes available at the faculty pilot plant.

researchers.name: Đorđe Đorđević
researchers.title: Assistant Professor

He was appointed Assistant Professor in 2021. His research focuses on measuring spatial accessibility to public transport, identifying transit deserts in mid-size urban areas, and evaluating equity outcomes of transit network changes. The group makes regular use of GTFS feeds, OpenStreetMap data, OpenTripPlanner, and QGIS in a Linux-based GIS laboratory at the Faculty. He teaches courses in Urban Transport Planning and Geographic Information Systems in Traffic Engineering at undergraduate and postgraduate level.

researchers.notes: Prefers projects where the University of Novi Sad team has clearly defined analytical tasks rather than advisory-only roles. Has limited availability for new commitments in the first half of 2025 due to teaching load during curriculum revision. researchers.name: Igor Krstić
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Igor Krstić completed his undergraduate and master's studies at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad, and received his PhD in 2009 from the same institution with a dissertation on demand forecasting under price uncertainty in Adriatic coastal tourism. He joined the Department of Management as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2021. His research group focuses on dynamic pricing models, revenue management algorithms, and the behavioural responses of consumers to price volatility in hotels, short-term rental platforms, and airline ancillary services. He teaches courses in strategic management, tourism economics, and quantitative methods for business. The group regularly uses statistical software environments and publicly available booking-platform datasets; no dedicated wet-lab or instrumentation is maintained.

researchers.name: Goran Nikolić
researchers.title: Research Associate
researchers.bio: Goran Nikolić completed his BSc and MSc degrees in Animal Science at the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, graduating with an MSc in 2013. He defended his PhD dissertation in 2018, focusing on fermentation kinetics and microbial community shifts in the rumen of dairy heifers fed increasing proportions of dried distillers' grains with solubles (DDGS). He joined the Department of Animal Science as a Research Associate in 2019. His group investigates how co-products from the bioethanol industry can be incorporated into ruminant diets without compromising rumen health or milk production potential. Nikolić teaches undergraduate courses in ruminant nutrition and conducts practical classes in feed analysis. He regularly uses DGGE, qPCR, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing for microbial profiling, and the department's in vitro gas production system for fermentation studies.

researchers.name: Branislav Žarković
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Branislav Žarković is a Full Professor at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad, where he leads research on credit risk and SME finance. Before joining academia, he served as head of risk at a regional bank from 2005 to 2012, giving him deep practical insight into lending operations and regulatory compliance. His current research focuses on credit scoring methodologies for thin-file borrowers, the integration of alternative data sources into underwriting models, and the design of explainable machine learning models that satisfy supervisory expectations. Professor Žarković has published extensively in peer-reviewed journals and conference proceedings and actively collaborates with fintech firms and financial regulators. He is open to industrial PhD supervision and joint research projects with industry partners.

He has been a Research Associate in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications since 2021. His group focuses on energy budgeting and lifetime prediction for battery-powered wireless sensor nodes, combining empirical cell testing with parametric degradation models. He teaches laboratory courses in analogue electronics and embedded systems. He regularly uses the department's battery cycling test bench, a Gamry impedance analyser, and a custom pulsed-load board developed in-house for WSN emulation.

researchers.name: Vladimir Ivanović
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation
researchers.bio: Vladimir Ivanović received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechanical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2005 and 2007 respectively, and his Ph.D. in Mechatronics from the same institution in 2013. His research group focuses on geometric accuracy of industrial manipulators, with particular emphasis on thermally induced positional drift, model-based error identification, and closed-loop kinematic recalibration executed during machine operation. The group maintains a laboratory equipped with a FARO laser tracker, a Renishaw telescoping ballbar, and two six-axis articulated robot arms used as testbeds. He teaches courses in Robot Kinematics, Sensor Systems, and Industrial Automation at undergraduate and graduate levels.

researchers.name: Milan Vojnović

researchers.name: Mina Obradović
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.bio: Mina Obradović completed her BSc and MSc in Mathematics and Computer Science at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2011 and 2013 respectively, and obtained her PhD from the same institution in 2018 with a thesis on rolling-horizon methods for disrupted bus fleet scheduling. She joined the Department of Mathematics and Informatics as a teaching assistant in 2014 and was appointed Assistant Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on combinatorial optimisation for transportation and logistics, with particular emphasis on real-time metaheuristics—large neighbourhood search, adaptive tabu search—applied to dynamic vehicle and crew scheduling under disruptions. She teaches courses in algorithms, operations research, and discrete mathematics. The group uses a small computing cluster shared with the department and accesses commercial solver licences through a university agreement.

researchers.industry_experience: Obradović participated in a six-month applied research engagement with a regional bus operator in 2022–2023, during which the rolling-horizon scheduling prototype was piloted on live operational data under a data processing agreement. researchers.name: Sofija Ristić
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.department: Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics)
researchers.bio: Sofija Ristić received her Dipl.Ing. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechanical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 1998 and 2002, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2007, with a dissertation on elastomeric gasket compression behaviour under cyclic thermal loading. She joined the Department of Machine Design and Mechanics as an assistant professor in 2008 and was promoted to full professor in 2019. Her group focuses on sealing system integrity in outdoor electromechanical enclosures, covering gasket and O-ring material selection, thermal-gradient-driven moisture ingress, and failure analysis of protection-class housings. She teaches courses in Machine Elements, Tribology, and Engineering Materials. The group regularly uses climate test chambers, a coordinate-measuring machine, and scanning electron microscopy facilities available at the faculty.

researchers.name: Aleksa Mamužić

researchers.department: Department of Administrative and Public Law
researchers.bio: Aleksa Mamužić diplomirao je na Pravnom fakultetu Univerziteta u Novom Sadu 2005. godine, gde je i magistrirao 2009. i odbranio doktorsku disertaciju 2014. godine, s temom ustavnih ograničenja podzakonskog normiranja u Srbiji. Od 2015. radi kao docent, a od 2021. kao vanredni profesor na Katedri za upravno i javno pravo. Istraživački rad fokusira mu se na ustavnopravne granice prenosa normativnih ovlašćenja na regulatorna tela i pitanje tehničkih standarda u srpskom pravnom poretku. Učestvovao je u analizama zakonodavnih reformi u okviru procesa pridruživanja EU. Predaje Ustavno pravo i Upravno pravo na osnovnim i master studijama. Koristi komparativno-pravnu metodu i analizu sudske prakse Ustavnog suda Srbije.

researchers.industry_experience: Mamužić je pružao pravne analize i mišljenja za dva domaća privredna udruženja u vezi sa usklađenošću tehničkih propisa sa ustavnim standardima, naročito u kontekstu usaglašavanja sa zahtevima EU tržišta. Nije bio angažovan kao advokatski savetnik.

Prikladne teme saradnje sa NTP kompanijama uključuju pravni okvir za puštanje tehničkih proizvoda na srpsko i EU tržište, pitanja standardizacije i ocenjivanja usaglašenosti, te pravnu analizu obaveza prema regulatornim agencijama.

researchers.name: Jelena Marković
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Jelena Marković is a Full Professor at the University of Novi Sad's Faculty of Technology, Department of Food Preservation Engineering. Her research integrates food engineering, packaging science, and predictive microbiology to extend the shelf life of perishable horticultural products, with a particular focus on Serbian soft fruits. She has extensive experience developing modified atmosphere packaging systems and mathematical models for microbial growth kinetics in cold-chain logistics. Professor Marković has collaborated with multiple Serbian fruit exporters on industrial packaging trials and serves as an academic partner on the FRESHROUTE innovation project targeting cold-chain optimization for berry exports. She is actively open to industrial PhD supervision and joint research projects with industry.

researchers.name: Marko Filipović
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry
researchers.bio: Marko Filipović completed his undergraduate and master's studies in Chemical Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2005 and 2007 respectively. He received his PhD in 2012 from the same institution, with a dissertation focused on viscosity-index modifiers in polyalphaolefin-based gear oils. Following a postdoctoral stay at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Ljubljana (2013–2014), he returned to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. His group investigates the tribochemical behaviour of synthetic and semi-synthetic gear lubricants, with particular emphasis on thermal-oxidative degradation pathways, boundary-film characterisation by AFM and XPS, and elastohydrodynamic film-thickness measurements. He teaches courses in Industrial Chemistry and Surface Chemistry. The group operates a four-ball tribometer, a rotating-disc rheometer, a differential scanning calorimeter, and has shared access to a scanning electron microscope and XPS spectrometer.

researchers.name: Emilija Mladenović
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.department: Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications
researchers.bio: Emilija Mladenović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2011 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2016, with a thesis on memory-effect modelling in wideband RF power amplifiers. She completed a research stay at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology in 2014–2015. She has been an Assistant Professor in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications since 2017. Her group works on behavioural modelling of nonlinear RF devices, digital pre-distortion algorithm development, and characterisation of power amplifiers under multi-carrier and OFDM excitation. She teaches courses in microwave electronics and digital signal processing for communications. The group uses a Rohde & Schwarz vector signal analyser, a two-tone and OFDM signal generation testbed, and custom MATLAB and Python DPD simulation environments.
